newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SLUMAN WINS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1988 PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SLUMAN WINS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1988 PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Jeff Sluman finally shed the label of one-win wonder on Sunday as he captured the Tucson Classic by a single stroke over U.S. Open champion Steve Jones at Tucson National.
Sluman, adding a second victory to his triumph at the 1988 PGA Championship, shot five-under-par 67 in the final round for a 13-under total of 275.
Jones, who like Sluman bogeyed the 72nd hole, shot 70 Sunday for 276.
"I couldn't possibly be any happier. I've got the monkey off my back," said Sluman, who took away $234,000.
Between wins Sluman played in 241 tournaments, had 43 top 10's, and eight second-place finishes, including three playoff losses.
"I wasn't sure if it was ever going to happen. But if I never won again, I don't think my career would have been considered a poor one. I think my peers respect me as a good player," said Sluman.
Tied for third place at 11 under par were overnight leader Brad Bryant, who shot 73, and last week's winner, Paul Stankowski, who posted a 71.
Sluman's 65-67 weekend scores of 12 under par were the best two rounds anyone in the tournament put together, but he could not have won without some help from Jones and Bryant.

Bryant began the day with a two-stroke lead, and had a 10-footer for eagle on the eighth hole to move four shots ahead. "I just choked my guts out on that putt," said Bryant of the missed eagle opportunity.

Bryant then dropped back into a tie for the lead when he hit a 3-wood tee shot into the water on the 10th hole and made double bogey. "I don't know what happened there, I must have just lost my concentration," said Bryant.

Jones led the tournament on Thursday and Friday at 10 under par, but played the last two days just two under par. "You're not going to win many tournaments if you can't shoot lower than that. I hung in there though, and had a chance to win with a birdie on the last hole," said Jones.
Instead of making birdie, Jones made bogey, though he nearly salvaged par and a playoff, with a 60-foot putt that shaved the hole.

Jones over-clubbed the approach shot on 18, his 6-iron ending up in the gallery, above and left of the hole. Jones tried to hit a high flop to the hole, but thinned the shot and finished 60-feet beyond, on the other side of the green.
Sluman said that the element of his game that may have prevented him from winning more has been his chipping. On Saturday he chipped-in twice for birdie, and didn't hit a bad chip on the weekend.
His only bogey came on the 18th.
"I was pretty nervous, and when you're really nervous and there's water on both sides of the fairway, you don't always put your best swing on it," said Sluman.
He ended up in the front bunker, and faced a six-foot, downhill, sidehill putt for par that missed the hole by a couple of inches.
"After that there was nothing to do but watch Steve. I was prepared for a playoff, but since my record is 0-4 in playoffs, I'm glad it didn't happen," said Sluman.
